content.thinking: I should swap "within about a minute" for "almost at once", and change "logged from {G5309.3}" to "logged over {G5309.3}". I'm also double-checking phrases like "the minute of {G971b.6}" for stray number-like wording, and I'll simplify it to "At {G971b.6}" just to be safe.

action_items.item: Add a pre-release check that runs the account page tests with monthly-spend-feature on, including a shopper with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out monthly-spend-feature, and other flags that change account pages, to a small share of shoppers first, and widen the rollout only while the account page error rate stays at its baseline.
Turn a newly switched-on flag back off automatically when the service's error rate rises soon after the change.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that returned server errors rose from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average while the service was broken, and peaked at {series_at_worst}. The service's own warning put the account page error rate as high as {Gbac1.5}, at {Gbac1.7}.
The account page requests failed because they raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors were logged over {G5309.3} and were not seen before the onset.

ruled_out.what: The flag change to an-unrelated-feature, switched on at {P2.1}. It came after the onset at {began}, and the service recovered when only monthly-spend-feature was reverted.

A deploy. No deploy came back from the day before the onset. As of {T10.1}, every replica ran one revision, and that revision was in place while account pages rendered normally and errors sat at their baseline before the onset.

causal_chain.step: The failing code runs only when monthly-spend-feature is on, and admin switched that flag on at {P1.1}. Before the onset the flag was off for every logged evaluation (G7e5d). At {G971b.6} most evaluations came back on (G971b), and every logged evaluation over {Gce95.4} came back on (Gce95). Once the flag was set back to off, the service was no longer at the incident's level from {T20.2}, and the action was judged confirmed.

When use_monthly_summary is true, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}, the line the logged error points to. This comes from Code-Fix's reading of the source.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary exposed a calculation that averages a shopper's spending over this month's purchases, and that calculation likely breaks when a shopper has bought before but not yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check was seen that ran the monthly summary path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month before monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Code-Fix's reading points only to an existing test for the lifetime-average case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The failing division would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production, and the incident would not have happened.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off for every logged evaluation to on for every logged evaluation almost at once. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers, with a check on the error rate, was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit failing account pages before the error rise showed, and the flag could have been turned back off before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: admin switched on a second flag, an-unrelated-feature, at {P2.1}, while the incident was under way. Reverting monthly-spend-feature alone brought the service back. Had the second change also caused failures, the revert would not have been enough and the cause would have been harder to pick out.
went_well: The Investigator tied the errors to the monthly-spend-feature change, which became leading candidate C1, {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and the change can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the service was no longer at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix and two new tests, PR #364, {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: No person was paged when the alert fired: no on-call incident was linked to it.

input.root_cause: When monthly-spend-feature is on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the shopper's total for the month by the number of purchases made this month. Nothing in the files Code-Fix read handles the case where that list is empty, so for a shopper who has bought before but not this month the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py and the page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The calculation that fails for shoppers with no purchases this month was still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make their account pages fail again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
